en: The Second Part of the Analysis of the Monks' Rules (Bhikkhuvibhaṅga)
1.12 Section on Compendium (Saṅgahitavāra) With respect to the offenses conditioned by engaging in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven classes of offenses are those offenses comprised?
With respect to the offenses conditioned by engaging in sexual intercourse, those offenses are comprised by four of the seven classes of offenses.

It may be included in the class of offenses involving defeat (pārājika), it may be included in the class of grave offenses (thullaccaya), it may be included in the class of offenses requiring expiation (pācittiya),

or it may be included in the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa)… [and so on]… With reference to disrespect, regarding the offense caused by voiding feces, urine, or spittle into water— by how many of the seven classes of offenses is that offense comprised?
In dependence on disrespect, for the purpose of voiding feces, urine, or spittle in water, an offense is comprised within one of the seven classes of offenses—
the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
The fourth section on inclusion is finished.
